true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The new downsize overload replaces the existing five-argument method in Ruby

Ruby does not overload methods by arity: defining `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Any existing caller using the prior public method signature will now raise `ArgumentError` rather than resize its image. Support both forms in one method (for example with optional arguments or splatting) or update every caller and preserve compatibility for plugin callers.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side upload limits no longer honor the configured per-type limits

`validateUploadedFile` now rejects every upload above 10 MB, regardless of whether it is an image or attachment and regardless of `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb`. Sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB will have those uploads rejected in the browser before the server sees them, and the displayed limit is incorrect. If a fixed pre-downsize ceiling is needed for images, it should be applied only to images while attachments continue to use their configured limit.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
API URL uploads are capped at 10 MB instead of the configured upload limit

Remote uploads supplied through the API are now downloaded with a hard 10 MB limit. This applies before the code knows whether the URL is an image that can be downsized, and therefore also blocks remote attachment uploads that the site's `max_attachment_size_kb` permits. It also prevents configured image limits above 10 MB from being used. Preserve the configured limit for non-images (and use an explicitly documented pre-downsize image ceiling if one is required).

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated URL-form host entries no longer match embedding requests

The migration inserts legacy host-list values directly into the new table, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s normalization callback. Existing supported values such as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` are therefore stored with their scheme/path, while `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` extracts only `example.com` and queries for an exact stored host. After upgrade those migrated hosts are never allowed, disabling embeds for affected sites. Normalize each legacy value to its hostname before insertion (and avoid raw SQL interpolation).

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when no category matches the old embed_category setting

The category lookup dereferences `execute(...)[0]['id']` without checking whether the query returned a row. `embed_category` defaults to an empty value and may also name a deleted/nonexistent category, so a normal installation with no configured embedding category produces an empty result and raises on `nil['id']`. This prevents the entire database migration from completing; handle an empty result and fall back to the uncategorized category before dereferencing it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting all allowed hosts no longer disables expansion of embedded posts

This removes the only check that embedding is configured without replacing it with `EmbeddableHost.exists?`. Consequently, if `embed_truncate` is enabled, any existing `TopicEmbed` remains expandable even after every allowed host has been removed. Host removal should disable embedding behavior; otherwise stale embed records can still expose the expansion UI and trigger remote content retrieval.

Hosts configured with a port can never be allowed

The validation explicitly permits values such as `example.com:3000`, and the callback leaves the port intact because it only removes schemes and paths. However `URI(host).host` drops the port before the exact database lookup, so a request from `http://example.com:3000` searches for `example.com` and cannot match the stored `example.com:3000`. Either normalize stored values to hostname-only or consistently include and compare the port.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row

`TopicUser.find_by` can return nil for a logged-in user who has permission to view a topic but has never visited it or otherwise had a topic-user record created. The route is publicly reachable by any logged-in user, not only recipients of the particular email. The subsequent `tu.notification_level` dereference raises `NoMethodError`, returning a 500 instead of allowing the notification preference to be set. Use `TopicUser.change` (which creates missing rows) or explicitly create/fetch the record before reading and saving it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Unsubscribe state change is exposed as a GET request

The new GET route invokes `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which immediately modifies the current user's TopicUser notification level. Because GET requests are not protected by Rails CSRF verification and `check_xhr` is explicitly skipped for this action, any third-party page can cause a logged-in visitor's browser to request a known topic's unsubscribe URL (for example via an image or navigation) and silently change that user's notification preference. Render a confirmation page on GET and require a CSRF-protected POST/PUT for the state change, or use a purpose-specific signed token if one-click email unsubscribe is required.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrent blocked-email checks lose match-count updates

`should_block?` reads `match_count`, increments it in Ruby, and saves the record. Multiple simultaneous signup attempts for the same blocked address can all read the same value and overwrite one another, so `match_count` and potentially the observed match state are inaccurate. Use an atomic database update such as `update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or locking/counter updates.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive and can be bypassed

The lookup compares the raw submitted email with the raw stored email. Email local/domain casing is commonly accepted by this application (and the domain restriction check is case-insensitive), so a blocked entry such as `spam@example.com` will not match a signup submitted as `Spam@Example.com` on the normal case-sensitive varchar comparison. Normalize emails consistently (for example with `Email.downcase(...).strip`) when storing and looking up blocked addresses, and enforce that normalization for existing/admin-created records as well.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Non-matching blocked-email checks return nil instead of false

When no record exists, `record && ...` evaluates to `nil`, not `false`. This contradicts the included `be_false` example for this path (which will fail under RSpec's strict false matcher) and makes the predicate's return type inconsistent. Return an explicit boolean, e.g. `!!record && ...`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin validation accepts unrelated origins that are URL substrings

The receiver treats an origin as trusted when it appears anywhere in `discourseUrl`. For example, if the forum URL is `https://forum.example.com/`, the distinct origin `https://forum.example.co` passes this check because it is a prefix substring. A page on such an origin can send `discourse-resize` messages and control the iframe height. Parse `discourseUrl` and compare `e.origin` for exact origin equality instead of using substring matching.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Concurrent imports of the same URL can fail on the unique index

The code performs a non-locking lookup and then creates the `TopicEmbed`; two retrieve jobs for the same URL can both see no row and both create posts before one loses on the unique `embed_url` index. The losing transaction raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and the job fails instead of returning the already-created embed. This is especially reachable because staff requests bypass throttling and scheduled feed polling can overlap retrieval. Handle the unique-conflict case (or use a locking/upsert strategy) and return/reload the winning embed.

Imported feed HTML bypasses Discourse sanitization

Imported content is stored with `cook_method: raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns that raw value without running the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `PollFeed` passes arbitrary RSS/Atom item content directly into this method, so a feed containing `<script>`, event-handler attributes, or dangerous URLs can persist executable HTML. The embed view then renders `post.cooked` with `raw`, making this stored XSS execute for visitors of the embedding site (and the imported post may also be exposed through normal topic views). Sanitize imported HTML with the same allowlist used for posts before storing/rendering it, rather than using raw HTML as a sanitizer bypass.

Relative links without a leading slash are not converted to source URLs

`absolutize_urls` claims to convert relative URLs, but it only rewrites values beginning with `/`. Valid relative values such as `images/photo.jpg`, `../next.html`, and `page.html` remain relative in the stored raw HTML. When rendered by Discourse, browsers resolve them relative to the Discourse embed page rather than the source article, causing imported links and images to point to nonexistent or unintended local Discourse paths. Resolve all non-absolute HTTP(S) URLs against the source URI, while preserving fragment/mailto/etc. behavior as appropriate.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
The small-action button no longer aligns to the right after its parent becomes flex

`.small-action` is now a flex container, so its direct `button` is a flex item and its existing `float: right` is ignored by CSS. The button will be laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge as before, which can visibly break the post-action row and make it overflow when the description is long. Give the button an appropriate flex alignment rule (for example `margin-left: auto`) rather than relying on float.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Website-name inclusion predicate is misnamed and never used

ActiveModel serializer inclusion predicates use the `include_<attribute>?` method name, as elsewhere in this serializer. This defines `include_website_name` without the question mark, so it is ignored and `website_name` is serialized for every response, including as `null` when no website exists. Rename it to `include_website_name?` so the newly introduced field follows the intended optional-attribute contract.

false_positives.candidate:
Derived website name bypasses TL0 profile-field restrictions

`website_name` is serialized independently of `website` and is not included in `untrusted_attributes`. For a trust-level-0 user viewed anonymously, `include_website?` suppresses the website URL, but the new attribute is still emitted and contains the website host and, for matching instance domains, the full path. The profile page will render that value even though the underlying website field is intentionally hidden, leaking restricted profile information. Apply the same visibility predicate to `website_name` (for example by adding it to `untrusted_attributes`) and add a TL0-with-website serialization test.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Quote author link no longer preserves the light-theme color

The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the light branch of the new `dark-light-choose` expression is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. This makes embedded-post author links substantially lighter in light themes, contrary to the intended dark-theme-only substitution. Keep the primary branch at 30% and use the complementary secondary value (70%) for the dark branch.

true_positives.golden_comment: This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Desktop group member names use a different light-theme shade

The group-member name was previously primary at 30% lightness, but the new expression uses primary 50% in its light branch. This unnecessarily changes the light-theme styling while also selecting secondary 50% rather than the complementary secondary 70% for dark themes. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

true_positives.golden_comment: In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mobile modal message length uses the wrong light and dark variants

This changes a previous `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to a light branch of primary 30% and a dark branch of secondary 70%. The light-theme appearance regresses, and the dark-theme value is the inverse of the intended complementary secondary value. The light branch should remain primary 70%, with secondary 30% selected for dark themes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.

Quote author link no longer preserves the light-theme color

The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the light branch of the new `dark-light-choose` expression is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. This makes embedded-post author links substantially lighter in light themes, contrary to the intended dark-theme-only substitution. Keep the primary branch at 30% and use the complementary secondary value (70%) for the dark branch.

true_positives.golden_comment: In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mobile group member names use a different light-theme shade

The old mobile group-member name color was primary at 30% lightness, but the replacement changes it to primary 50% and secondary 50%. This regresses the existing light-theme contrast and does not apply the complementary secondary 70% needed in dark themes. Preserve the primary 30% branch and use secondary 70% for the dark branch.

false_positives.candidate:
Mobile topic-map heading loses its intended emphasis

The previous heading color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but this replacement uses 50% for both branches. As a result, topic-map headings become much more muted in light themes and do not receive the expected secondary 80% counterpart in dark themes. true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pagination creates a phantom page for exact multiples of the page size

`totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, so a group with exactly 50 members (or any exact multiple of `limit`) reports two pages. The Next control remains enabled, requests offset 50, and displays an empty member list. This also occurs after deleting the final member on a partially filled last page when the count becomes an exact multiple. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (while preserving the zero-member special case) and clamp/reload the offset as needed.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pagination creates a phantom page for exact multiples of the page size

`totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, so a group with exactly 50 members (or any exact multiple of `limit`) reports two pages. The Next control remains enabled, requests offset 50, and displays an empty member list. This also occurs after deleting the final member on a partially filled last page when the count becomes an exact multiple. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (while preserving the zero-member special case) and clamp/reload the offset as needed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locale files are not loaded for translations outside controller requests

The translation accelerator only loads `config.locale` before calling the backend. `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` performs fallback lookups by invoking the backend directly for the fallback locale, so it does not re-enter `I18n.translate` and therefore does not load that locale's YAML file. The new `ApplicationController#set_locale` works around this only for controller actions; jobs, mailers, models, rake tasks, and any translation performed before that callback can fall back to an unloaded default/en locale and return missing-translation errors even when the fallback translation exists. Loading every locale in `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]` as part of translation (or otherwise ensuring this globally) is needed.

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Conditional passkeys are no longer initialized for anonymous login

`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` returns false whenever no user has been selected. Consequently, the initial username/password page does not call `fillContextForm`, which is the call that sets `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, creates/stores the WebAuthn challenge, and supplies the WebAuthn form attributes. This disables conditional/passkey authentication before a username is entered, defeating discoverable-passkey login. The same user-null guard in the error challenge path also removes passkeys after an invalid username submission. The pre-existing behavior intentionally initialized the conditional UI when passkeys were enabled even with no selected user; retain that behavior while additionally supporting the selected-user reauthentication case.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Advanced negative-offset path uses unsupported Django queryset slicing

The new advanced path passes a negative `start_offset` directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing or slicing and raise an error rather than interpreting it as reverse/boundary pagination. Cursor parsing accepts negative offsets (`Cursor.from_string` converts the offset with `int`), so an authorized caller can cause the optimized audit-log endpoint to return a 500 with a cursor such as `0:-1:0`; the advertised reverse-pagination feature is not functional.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs

`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the ordered field value. The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so each result has a `datetime` value and cursor construction raises `TypeError` on the first optimized request. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, this class neither converts datetimes to a numeric cursor value nor converts cursor values back to datetimes for the ranged query. Consequently, an administrator requesting `optimized_pagination=true` receives a 500 rather than audit-log results.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Optimized paginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry datetime keys

This endpoint orders by `-datetime`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the value of that field. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a `datetime`, not a numeric value, so an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` will raise a TypeError while constructing cursors and return a 500. The optimized paginator needs datetime key conversion equivalent to `DateTimePaginator`, or this endpoint must continue to use a datetime-aware paginator.

false_negatives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Deploying this script against existing set-backed buffers causes Redis WRONGTYPE failures

Existing buffered segment keys were created as Redis SETs by the previous version. This script now executes `ZCARD` and `ZUNIONSTORE` on those same keys. Redis does not permit ZSET commands on SET values, so any trace with an in-flight pre-deployment buffer will make the script fail with WRONGTYPE, failing span processing until the old key expires (up to `redis_ttl`, normally an hour). A rollout-compatible migration/fallback or a versioned key namespace is required.

Reducing redirect traversal depth can split deep traces into separate segments

The redirect-chain traversal limit was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000. For a trace whose parent/child buffers form a chain deeper than 1,000, resolution stops before reaching the actual segment root; subsequent spans are merged into an intermediate buffer and flushed as a separate segment. This changes the prior supported depth and produces incorrect segment assignments for deep traces.

max_segment_spans configuration is no longer honored

`max_segment_spans` remains a constructor parameter and instance attribute, but the only enforcement was removed from `_load_segment_data`; the Lua script instead always retains 1000 members. Deployments that configure a different limit now silently get a hard-coded retention policy, and segments over the configured limit are emitted rather than skipped as before. Either pass the configured limit to Lua and enforce it there, or remove/change the public configuration deliberately.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the outer dataset rather than the dataset being queried

`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, including calls made for dashboard discover splits, but passes the closed-over original `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. For example, a metrics-enhanced dashboard that is split into a `discover` error query evaluates eligibility as a metrics dataset and never applies upsampling. The decision needs to use `scoped_dataset` so the columns match the actual query being executed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Aliased count aggregations are not upsampled

Only a column whose entire text is exactly `count()` is transformed. Valid selected aggregations such as `count() as errors` remain raw counts even when every project is allowlisted, yielding inconsistent and incorrect results depending solely on whether the caller aliases the aggregation. Preserve and transform supported count aliases (and their output aliases) when rewriting query columns.

Allowlist changes leave cached count behavior stale with no invalidation integration

Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, and although `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is provided, this PR does not connect it to changes of `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`. Consequently, enabling or disabling a project can continue returning raw or upsampled counts until TTL expiry, including returning upsampled counts after sampling has been disabled. Invalidate affected keys when the option changes, or avoid caching configuration whose changes must take effect immediately.

Discover upsampling is enabled for mixed or negated event-type queries

The discover eligibility check is a raw substring match for `event.type:error`, which does not establish that the query contains only error events. Queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` and `!event.type:error` both match and will replace `count()` with `sum(sample_weight)`. Transaction rows do not have error sampling weights, so their events are omitted or incorrectly weighted, producing incorrect counts. Parse/inspect the query condition and enable this only when it constrains the result set exclusively to error events.

Upsampled counts truncate fractional sample weights

The custom aggregate wraps `sum(sample_weight)` in `toInt64`. Sample weights derived from arbitrary client sampling rates are not necessarily integral (for example, a 0.3 sample rate produces an expected weight near 3.33), so truncating the aggregate silently undercounts sampled errors. Return the sum as a numeric/float result unless the stored sample-weight contract guarantees integral values.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error IDs can be paired with the wrong nodestore event when an event is missing

`nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a mapping, but the implementation pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` by position. If the backend omits a missing node from the mapping (as multi-get implementations commonly do), all subsequent values shift and error details are attributed to the wrong replay error IDs. Look up each result by its generated node ID and retain the corresponding original event ID rather than zipping with mapping values.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feature-flagged table visualization discards all dashboard query results

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the new `TableWidgetVisualization` is always given `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` object instead of `result.data`, `result.meta`, and the widget fields. Consequently every table widget for organizations with this feature renders an empty table regardless of the query result, replacing the existing populated `StyledSimpleTableChart`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mutual exclusion of age and timestamp fails for zero values

The checks use `self.initial_data.get(...)`, which treats `0` as absent. Thus a request with `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes validation even though it mixes the two mutually exclusive reporting formats. Presence should be checked with key membership (or object-level validated data), not truthiness.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
Browser report validation permits reports with neither timestamp nor age

Both spec-specific fields are optional and validation only runs when one is supplied, so a report containing neither `timestamp` nor `age` is accepted and counted. The endpoint claims to support the two formats, each of which requires its respective timing field; accepting neither lets malformed reports pollute the collection metrics. Add object-level validation requiring exactly one of the two fields.

Falsy custom cell render results incorrectly invoke the fallback renderer

The documented renderer contract says fallback rendering occurs when a custom renderer returns `undefined`, but this code uses `if (cell)`. Intentional valid React render results such as `0`, an empty string, or `false` are treated as absent and replaced by the default field renderer. Test specifically for `cell !== undefined` (and make the same correction in the header renderer at line 31).

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code consumption is not atomic, allowing code reuse under concurrent logins

The code reads and decrypts the complete backup-code list, validates a code, and then writes a modified copy without any conditional update, transaction isolation, or version check. Two concurrent credential requests using the same code can both read the pre-consumption list and both authenticate successfully; requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's update and restore a previously consumed code. This violates the advertised one-time-use property of backup codes and can result in multiple successful sessions from a single stolen code. Consume the code with an atomic/optimistic conditional update (or store individually hashed codes with a uniqueness/consumption state) and reject a request whose stored state changed before its update.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
The new backup-code authentication and one-time-use behavior is not tested

The added tests only exercise displaying the backup-code screen and downloading/copying its UI. They never authenticate with a generated backup code, verify that a valid code works, verify rejection of an invalid code, or verify that a successfully used code cannot be reused; disabling 2FA with a backup code is also untested. These are the core security-sensitive paths introduced by this PR, so regressions such as failing backup login or non-consuming codes will ship undetected.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet fallback dereferences an absent destination calendar

`evt.destinationCalendar` is optional and is explicitly constructed as `null`/empty for bookings without a selected destination calendar. Destructuring it yields `undefined`, but the following condition reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Creating a Google Meet event without a destination calendar will therefore throw before any calendar/video event is created (and may also fail type checking under strict null checks). Guard this access, e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google updates lose the configured calendar when a legacy reference has no external calendar ID

When `externalCalendarId` is absent, the fallback now searches for a destination whose `externalId === externalCalendarId`; since that value is undefined, this always produces undefined. The previous behavior used the event's destination calendar. As a result, updating/rescheduling bookings with older references that lack `externalCalendarId` sends an undefined `calendarId` to Google instead of updating the selected destination calendar. Fall back to the destination associated with this credential (or the primary calendar) rather than searching for an undefined ID.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Collective host calendars are discarded when the primary organizer has no destination calendar

The event initializes `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. For a collective booking, other hosts' calendars are collected in `teamDestinationCalendars`, but `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` becomes a no-op when that initial value is null. Thus a collective whose organizer has no calendar configured but whose additional hosts do have calendars creates no events for those hosts, which is one of the cases this change is intended to support. Initialize this field to an empty array before appending host calendars.

Each destination is created with the full destination list, causing non-Google providers to target the first host's calendar

The loop invokes `createEvent` once per destination/credential, but passes the same unfiltered `event` each time. `CalendarManager.createEvent` only forwards the credential ID; it does not forward `destination.externalId`. Google happens to look up the matching credential, but the Office365, Lark, and CalDAV services all select `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. Consequently, when creating a collective event for a second host, those services use the second host's credential against the first host's external calendar (usually failing due to permissions, or creating in the wrong calendar). Pass the current destination to the service or provide each invocation an event whose destination list contains only that destination; providers must not infer the target from index zero.

Recurring cancellation only selects the first calendar reference of each occurrence

For every updated recurring booking, the code uses `.find()` to obtain a single calendar reference, despite this PR now creating one reference per host destination. It then attempts that one reference with every calendar credential, while ignoring all remaining references for the occurrence. In a collective recurring booking, events created for secondary hosts are therefore not deleted on cancellation (and the primary event receives redundant deletion attempts). Iterate each updated booking's calendar references and invoke deletion using that reference's credential/calendar ID.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The permissive sync schema strips the expiry field supplied by the credential service

`minimumTokenResponseSchema` is a Zod object and Zod objects strip unknown properties by default. The computed keys do not make it a catch-all schema, so a sync response such as `{ access_token, expiry_date }` is parsed down to just `access_token`; the function then injects a fake refresh token. Callers that require expiry information, notably Zoom's `newTokens.expires_in`, persist an invalid/NaN expiry and subsequently try to refresh again using the fake refresh token. Use `.passthrough()`/`z.record` as appropriate and preserve the documented expiry field, or normalize it explicitly for each provider.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google credential updates store Zod's SafeParse result instead of credential keys

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the complete `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but this value is written directly to `Credential.key`. Google credential loading later parses `credential.key` as the Google token object, so after the first refresh the stored wrapper no longer has top-level `access_token`, `refresh_token`, or expiry fields and the integration becomes unusable. Persist `key.data` after checking success, not the SafeParse result.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential-sync responses are returned in a shape incompatible with several refresh callers

The sync branch returns the raw Fetch Response, whereas the original refresh functions return provider SDK/Axios results. Google Calendar reads `res.data`, and HubSpot, Zoho CRM, and Zoho Bigin all read fields through `.data`; a Fetch Response has neither parsed data nor those token fields. With syncing enabled, token refresh for these integrations therefore reads undefined values or throws instead of using the synchronized access token. The helper must normalize the sync response to the contract expected by each caller (or all callers must explicitly parse `response.json()`).

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

Google Calendar reads `res.data`, and HubSpot, Zoho CRM, and Zoho Bigin all read fields through `.data`; a Fetch Response has neither parsed data nor those token fields. With syncing enabled, token refresh for these integrations therefore reads undefined values or throws instead of using the synchronized access token. true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zoho Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal.com user ID to the sync endpoint

`refreshOAuthTokens` expects its third argument to be the credential owner user ID and sends it as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, which is the database credential primary key. The self-hosted credential service will look up the wrong user (or no user), so Bigin refresh fails or can retrieve another user's token when numeric IDs happen to overlap. Pass `credential.userId` through this refresh path instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Concurrent credential webhooks can create duplicate credentials

The endpoint implements an upsert as a `findFirst` followed by a separate create/update, but the lookup is not protected by a transaction or a unique `(userId, appId)` constraint. Two simultaneous webhook deliveries for a user without a credential can both observe no row and create separate credentials. Several integration paths use `findFirst`, so which synced credential is used becomes nondeterministic and stale credentials remain active. Use an enforced unique key with upsert, or serialize/retry this operation.

Salesforce service references Prisma without importing it

The newly added refresh logic calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file has no `@calcom/prisma` import. TypeScript compilation fails with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`, blocking builds that include the app-store package.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest blacklist can be bypassed by email casing

Blacklist entries are normalized to lowercase, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. Since valid email addresses may contain uppercase characters, submitting `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a blacklist entry for `blocked@example.com` and creates/sends an invitation to that address. Normalize submitted addresses (and attendee duplicate comparisons) before applying policy checks.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team administrators and owners are incorrectly denied access

The authorization flag requires `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. Team roles are distinct, so a normal team administrator is not an owner and a normal owner is not an administrator; neither can satisfy this condition unless the helper methods deliberately overlap. This makes the advertised team-admin/owner access path unusable for bookings they do not personally organize or attend. Use an OR between the role checks.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Existing attendees can receive a new-booking email when mixed with new guests

The database write correctly filters `guests` into `uniqueGuests`, but notifications are called with the original `guests` array. If a request contains both an already-attending address and a new address, `sendAddGuestsEmails` classifies the existing attendee as a newly added guest and sends it an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (including a calendar invite) instead of the guest-added update. Pass `uniqueGuests` to the mail sender.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The API accepts duplicate guests and can fail or create duplicate attendees

Duplicate validation exists only in the dialog, while the public tRPC schema and handler do not deduplicate `guests`. `uniqueGuests` only excludes attendees that existed before the request, so a direct request such as `["guest@example.com", "guest@example.com"]` retains both entries and passes both to `createMany`. Depending on the database constraint this either produces duplicate attendee rows and notifications or fails the whole mutation with a database error. Validate/deduplicate on the server before writing.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest-add notifications ignore event-type email opt-out settings

`sendAddGuestsEmails` sends organizer, team-member, existing-attendee, and new-attendee emails unconditionally. Other standard booking notification paths check `disableStandardEmails.all.host` and `.attendee`, but this new path neither accepts event metadata nor performs those checks. Consequently, adding a guest overrides an event type's configured host/attendee email suppression and sends notifications users explicitly disabled.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Guest list size is unbounded

The mutation accepts an unbounded array of email addresses. Any authorized attendee can submit a very large payload, causing an equally large database insert, calendar attendee update, and email fan-out; the latter also sends update emails to every existing attendee. This is an application-level mail/third-party API abuse vector and can exhaust request resources. Add a server-side maximum guest count (and ideally a matching UI limit).

Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings through the API

The handler updates any booking ID after authorization and never checks booking status or whether the event is still active. Although the list UI only exposes edit actions for accepted bookings, callers can invoke this mutation directly for cancelled/rejected/pending (and past) bookings. It then adds attendee records and sends calendar `REQUEST`/confirmed emails for an event that may no longer exist. Enforce the allowed booking state server-side before modifying attendees.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry count updates can be lost when cron executions overlap

The handler reads `retryCount` in `findMany` and later writes `reminder.retryCount + 1`. Concurrent or overlapping cron requests can select the same reminder with count 0, both fail scheduling, and both write 1. The reminder has then failed twice but is treated as having failed once and continues being retried; concurrent executions can also repeatedly attempt the same SMS. Use an atomic database increment (and ideally atomically claim/transition an unscheduled reminder) rather than a stale read-modify-write value.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry cleanup is not restricted to SMS reminders

The new `OR` branch deletes every `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, regardless of its method, scheduled state, or scheduled date. This cron is specifically the SMS scheduler and the previous cleanup was scoped to `method: SMS`; as written, any email/WhatsApp reminder (or another producer using this field later) with a retry count above one will be silently deleted by the SMS cron. Restrict the retry-count branch to unscheduled SMS reminders so this job cannot remove unrelated workflow work.

false_positives.candidate:
Exception-path retry update has the same lost-update race

The catch path also persists a value calculated from the count captured before scheduling. Two overlapping failing invocations overwrite each other with the same value, so exceptions do not reliably advance the retry limit either. This path should use the same atomic increment/claim mechanism as the non-throwing failed-response path.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
Removing findMany breaks the service's existing public API

`findMany` was a public method on `InsightsBookingService` and was removed rather than migrated or retained. The replacement, `getBaseConditions`, only returns a SQL fragment and does not accept or apply the caller's `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs` (including select, pagination, ordering, and additional where clauses). No production call sites are updated in this PR, so existing consumers will either fail TypeScript compilation (`service.findMany is not a function`) or must be rewritten outside this change. Retain a compatible query method or update every consumer as part of the migration.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook test script uses a macOS-only sed invocation

`sed -i '' -E` is BSD/macOS syntax; GNU sed (the standard on Linux development machines and CI containers) interprets the empty argument differently and fails to update the env file. The script therefore cannot perform its advertised setup on Linux. Use a portable replacement strategy or select the `sed -i` arguments based on the platform.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting cache does not invalidate the displayed cache-status query

The delete mutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback and never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. In this wrapper `onChanged` is optional, and even callers that supply it are not required to refetch this query. Consequently, after a successful deletion the card can continue displaying the old `cacheUpdatedAt` value and the "Delete cached data" action until a manual reload or another unrelated refetch. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` on delete settlement/success (as the disconnect mutation already does).

Expired cache rows are reported as an active cache status

`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups every CalendarCache row for a credential without filtering on `expiresAt`. Cache reads treat rows whose `expiresAt` is in the past as unusable, but this status API will still return their newest `updatedAt`, causing the UI to claim a cache exists and show a stale "Last updated" timestamp for up to however long expired rows remain in the database. The status query should restrict rows to unexpired entries, consistent with `getCachedAvailability`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cancellation does not wait for workflow reminders to be marked cancelled

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are asynchronous, but the calls inside these `forEach` loops are neither awaited nor collected into the later `Promise.all`. Previously the handler awaited the Prisma reminder deletions; now it can return successfully before email reminders have been marked `cancelled` for the cron job. In particular, in serverless/request teardown scenarios this work may not complete, and provider/database errors are detached from the cancellation request. Collect and await these operations before completing booking cancellation.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Expired cancelled reminders are deleted before SendGrid cancellation can be retried

The initial `deleteMany` removes every email reminder whose scheduled date has passed, including reminders with `cancelled: true`. If the cancellation request failed during a prior cron run (or one failed request aborted the loop at line 75), the next run deletes the only local record before attempting to cancel its SendGrid batch. The SendGrid scheduled send remains active and can still be delivered. Cancelled reminders must be excluded from this cleanup until the provider cancellation succeeds, or cancellation must be processed before cleanup with durable retry handling.

SendGrid client used for cancellation is never configured with the API key

This module configures `sgMail` with `SENDGRID_API_KEY`, but it never calls `client.setApiKey(...)` before using `client.request` to cancel scheduled sends at line 57. `@sendgrid/client` has separate configuration from `@sendgrid/mail`, so the new cancellation request can fail authentication and leave the SendGrid email scheduled. Configure the client in this module before making cancellation requests.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

Reschedule does not await calendar imports or external deletions

`forEach(async ...)` discards every callback promise. As a result, this function sends the reschedule email and returns success without waiting for `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`; an import failure is also outside the surrounding `try/catch` and becomes an unhandled rejection. This can leave the prior calendar event undeleted while the booking is already marked cancelled. Replace the `forEach` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (and keep it inside the error handling).

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule does not await calendar imports or external deletions

`forEach(async ...)` discards every callback promise. As a result, this function sends the reschedule email and returns success without waiting for `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`; an import failure is also outside the surrounding `try/catch` and becomes an unhandled rejection. This can leave the prior calendar event undeleted while the booking is already marked cancelled. Replace the `forEach` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (and keep it inside the error handling).

false_positives.candidate:
All integration chunks are started eagerly when appStore is imported

Each `import("./...")` expression is evaluated while constructing `appStore`, so importing this module immediately starts loading every app package. This does not defer loading until a particular integration is selected; it can fetch/initialize all optional integration chunks on requests that only need one (or none), undermining the intended lazy-loading benefit and increasing startup/request resource use. Store import functions (for example `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and invoke only the selected one.

Request-reschedule returns before imported integrations are deleted

The async callback passed to `forEach` is not collected or awaited. Since it now awaits `getCalendar` before calling `deleteEvent`, the mutation proceeds to send email/webhooks and resolves before deletion has even started; failures while importing an app are not propagated or handled. Await a mapped set of deletion promises (or use an awaited `for...of`) so the cancellation side effect is completed or handled before reporting the reschedule request.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Date-override availability does not require the whole event to fit in the override

The override check only rejects a slot whose end is at/before the override start or whose start is after the override end. It never rejects a slot that starts within the override but ends after its end (and also permits a slot that begins before the override and crosses its start). For example, with a 10:00-11:00 override and a 60-minute event, a 10:30 slot is considered available even though the host is only available until 11:00. This can advertise and book fixed hosts outside their date override.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

false_positives.candidate:
Fixed-host working hours are compared against UTC slot clock values

`slotStartTime` is explicitly converted to UTC, but its UTC weekday/hour/minutes are compared directly with `workingHour.days`, `startTime`, and `endTime`, which represent the host schedule's local clock values. `organizerTimeZone` is not used for this working-hours comparison. A fixed host in a non-UTC timezone can therefore pass or fail the new fixed-host availability filter at the wrong local time; for example, a UTC+05:30 host's 18:00 local boundary is checked as 12:30 against an 18:00 local end. The check also sets `end` equal to the slot start, so it does not verify that the event duration fits before the working-hours end. This can expose round-robin slots when a fixed host is unavailable.

The added test does not cover fixed-host round-robin overrides

The stated primary regression is a round-robin event with a fixed host, but the added test is a single-user event and only exercises slot generation. It never exercises `checkIfIsAvailable` for fixed hosts, where this PR adds the override and working-hours filtering. Consequently, regressions that still offer a round-robin slot while its fixed host is outside an override are not caught.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Legacy or pipeline-created integrations without sender metadata cause a 500

The comparison indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` unconditionally. Integrations created by the normal pipeline do not populate `sender` in `build_integration`, and integrations created before this change also lack it (the updated basic-flow test still asserts metadata without `sender`). If such an active integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed and is installed again, this path raises `KeyError` instead of returning the installation failure response. Handle absent sender metadata explicitly and provide a safe validation/migration path.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

false_positives.candidate:
New installations bypass the GitHub installer identity check

When there is no existing `Integration` row for the supplied installation ID, this branch immediately advances the pipeline without comparing the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user to the app installation sender. The integration is then created from the installation ID in a later pipeline step. Consequently, a Sentry organization administrator who knows or obtains another GitHub App installation ID can authorize with their own GitHub account and attach an installation that has not yet been recorded by Sentry (for example before its webhook is processed) to their Sentry organization, potentially gaining Sentry-mediated access to that installation's repositories. The validation must also be enforced for the first creation of an integration, using a trustworthy installer identity rather than only existing webhook-backed records.

OAuth transport and user-info failures escape as server errors

Only parsing the access-token response is guarded. `safe_urlopen` can raise for a GitHub/network HTTP failure, and `get_user_info` can raise when the returned token is rejected or the user API is unavailable. Either exception escapes the pipeline and returns a 500 rather than the intended invalid-installation response. Catch the expected HTTP/API exceptions around both the token exchange and user lookup and return `error(...)` so invalid, reused, or failed OAuth codes fail safely as described.

true_positives.golden_comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`queued` is evaluated once when the module is imported

`timezone.now()` is evaluated while defining the dataclass, so every `AssignmentSource` constructed without an explicit `queued` value receives the same import-time timestamp rather than the time that webhook-triggered assignment was queued. This makes the context metadata incorrect for the lifetime of a worker process (and would break any future age/ordering logic based on this field). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance captures its own creation time.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.

Registered metric-alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated

`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now inherits `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its required abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). false_positives.candidate:
Removing the existing mark_failed module helpers breaks their import contract
